articles.title: MULTI-STEP PAYWALLS: WHY THEY CAN CONVERT BETTER AND HOW TO TEST YOUR OWN
articles.summary: This article explores multi-step paywalls for subscription apps, showing how sequential screens reduce cognitive load and build trust. Citing industry data, it explains how multi-page flows outperform single-screen options in conversion, outlines key design patterns, and highlights metrics like lifetime value and refunds.

articles.title: BLAST OPEN THE BOTTLENECK BETWEEN YOUR AI IDEAS AND PRODUCTION
articles.summary: While AI has lowered the cost of generating ideas, expert judgment to safely validate and deploy them has become the main bottleneck. Enterprises must shift focus to trust engineering and validation frameworks. Otherwise, they will realize minimal value from their agentic AI investments.

articles.title: STOP ASKING USERS WHAT THEY WANT
articles.summary: Product engineers should avoid asking users what features they want, focusing instead on uncovering underlying problems through targeted interviews. Drawing on user research, this article details questioning techniques to understand user context, actual behavior, core motivations, and the true value of features.

articles.title: THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A HOBBY PRODUCT AND SOMETHING OTHERS MIGHT USE?
articles.summary: The creator of Paper Drum teaches product owners how to listen to users, yet caught himself pitching features and troubleshooting during user interviews intended for product testing.

articles.title: PLAID BUILT $382K IN PIPELINE FROM ONE TLDR PLACEMENT
articles.summary: Close Q4 with proof. TLDR reaches 8 million tech readers across 14 newsletters. Book a Q4 campaign [11].

articles.title: EVALS FOR PRODUCT MANAGERS: WRITE THE BAR, THEN THE PRODUCT
articles.summary: For AI products, product managers should use structured evals as primary specifications instead of vague requirements. This approach involves defining quality standards, establishing clear pass-or-fail criteria, setting numerical launch bars before reviewing scores, and maintaining a human-in-the-loop evaluation process.

articles.title: FROM PROBLEM TO FEATURE: SCOPING WORK
articles.summary: This guide outlines a practical approach to scoping software development by breaking problems into independent, valuable features rather than monolithic tasks. It explains how to define business problems, write implementation-independent acceptance criteria, and handle edge cases like technical debt and estimation.

articles.title: JAMMED TYPEWRITERS
articles.summary: While AI speeds up development, legacy processes designed to ration engineering time now create bottlenecks. Citing Faros AI data on rising task completions but slower deployments, the author compares outdated rituals to the QWERTY keyboard and urges teams to re-evaluate their workflows.

articles.title: WHAT CHANGED THIS YEAR
articles.summary: Amy Mitchell reset her product management writing to focus on personal learning and real-world problem-solving. Integrating AI tools transformed how she investigates challenges, leading her to abandon daily notes and paid content to explore the practical realities of product work.
